subject: plandex
title: Ellipsis-anchored structured edits resolved against tree-sitter node maps with unique/fuzzy replacement fallbacks
one_why: The '// ... existing code ...' sparse-edit format this project popularized is backed by a real parser-anchored resolver (findNextAnchor walks tree-sitter nodes to match fragments) plus deterministic fallbacks, and it is the corpus's best-tested edit path -- the model emits only changed regions, which is the token-economy lever for large codebases.

subject: plandex
title: Genuine property-table tests exist but nothing runs them in CI
evidence: .github/workflows/ contains only docker-publish.yml; 2,511 LOC in 6 *_test.go vs 74,240 non-test; promptfoo eval POC at test/evals/promptfoo-poc/ unwired
one_why: Test quality is not the problem -- TestStructuredReplacements and TestBufferOrStream assert real behavior -- but zero CI wiring means even those regress silently; a minimal go test workflow would monetize tests that already exist.

subject: plandex
title: Every plan gets its own server-side git repo; rewind/checkout/version are git shas
one_why: Checkpointing agent state as commits in a dedicated per-plan repo (not the user's working repo, not a snapshot dir) gives branch/rewind/diff semantics for free and composes with auto-revert on failed runs; MIT-licensed so the approach is directly liftable.

subject: plandex
title: Automode presets gate exec by config only -- shell runs via sh -c with nothing underneath
evidence: app/shared/plan_config.go:130-143 (AutoModeFull sets CanExec+AutoExec); app/cli/lib/apply.go:399 (exec.Command(shell,"-c",scriptPath)); no sandbox/policy code in app/cli or app/shared
one_why: Defaults are honest (Semi, manual exec) and security.md overclaims nothing, but full-auto mode is exactly the 'tested approval, nothing underneath' failure with no tests: one prompt injection in loaded context executes unsandboxed; contrast codex's 10-rung kernel enforcement.

subject: plandex
title: On token overflow, search stored conversation summaries for the newest timestamp that fits, graft it, keep the tail
one_why: Reactive rather than projected compaction, but the graft search (pick an existing ConvoSummary whose timestamp divides convo under the effective max, error only if none fits) makes compaction idempotent across retries and avoids re-summarizing the same prefix -- a detail single-shot auto-compact designs miss.

subject: plandex
title: Exec failure triggers capped rollback -> tell-with-output -> rebuild -> re-exec recursion
evidence: app/cli/plan_exec/apply_exec.go:26-168 (onExecFail closure re-sets AutoExec/ExecEnabled, passes failure output into TellPlan, attempt counter, ApplyRollbackPlan)
one_why: The repair loop is explicit, bounded by AutoDebugTries, and always rolls back the failed apply before retrying -- crash-safe iteration structure worth copying even though there is no loop-detection breaker above it.

subject: plandex
title: Static ephemeral cache breakpoints at every planning/implementation phase boundary in the system prompt
one_why: Phase-structured prompts (planning-shared vs phase-only vs implementation parts) make cache breakpoint placement mechanical instead of ad hoc; no warming or hit-rate telemetry, so it is marking discipline, not pi-grade cache management.
